The island’s coastal zones are mostly low-elevation areas. The railway lines in the figure are mainly distributed along the low and flat coastal zones on the periphery of Hainan Island, forming an approximately ring shape around the island, rather than crossing the central highlands. Reasoning: Railway route selection usually tries to avoid mountainous areas with large terrain undulations and high engineering difficulty, and gives priority to passing through coastal plains with lower and flatter terrain and more concentrated populations and cities.
